    # Nextflow Pipeline: RNA-seq QC

    **Difficulty:** 🟡 Intermediate  ·  **SDK:**   ·  **Updated:** 2026-05-15

    **Capabilities demonstrated:** [workflows](../../capabilities/workflows.md) [build-services](../../capabilities/build-services.md) [domain-bio](../../capabilities/domain-bio.md)

    [:material-github: View full repo on GitHub](https://github.com/ivcap-works/ivcap-rnaseq-nextflow){ .md-button }

    ---

    This repository is a **minimal, worked example** showing how to **package a Nextflow pipeline** so it can be **deployed and executed on IVCAP**.

The pipeline implemented here is based on the Nextflow training material:

  • https://training.nextflow.io/latest/nf4_science/rnaseq/03_multi-sample/

In this repo the pipeline focuses on a paired-end RNA-seq QC workflow using:

  • FastQC (initial QC)
  • Trim Galore (adapter trimming + post-trim QC)
  • MultiQC (aggregated QC report)

Note: There is a HISAT2 module present, but alignment is currently commented out in main.nf.

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
• Repository layout (high level)
  • Prerequisites
  • Run locally
  • Deploy to IVCAP
  • Actual deployment)
  • Test an IVCAP job request
  • Notes / known quirks
  • More instructions will follow

docs.title: Repository layout (high level)
docs.text:
• main.nf — Nextflow entrypoint
  • nextflow.config — Nextflow configuration (Docker enabled, reports/timeline/trace enabled)
  • modules/ — DSL2 modules used by the workflow
  • data/ — example inputs for local runs
  • data/paired-end.csv — example samplesheet used by default
  • schema_input.json — JSON schema describing the sample input file structure (used by the IVCAP controller)
  • ivcap-service.yaml — IVCAP service definition template (references the packaged pipeline artifact)
  • ivcap-tool.yaml — JSON schema (AI tool) definition for the IVCAP job request payload (parameters + samplesheet)
  • tests/simple_rnaseq_ivcap.json — example IVCAP job request
  • Makefile — convenience targets for running, packaging, deploying, and testing

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Nextflow (and Docker if running with containers)
  • IVCAP CLI (for deployment/testing against an IVCAP environment)
  • Install instructions: https://github.com/ivcap-works/ivcap-cli

docs.title: Run locally
docs.text:
This repo is configured to run with Docker.

$ make run
rm -rf .nextflow* work results
nextflow run "main.nf" \
        -c nextflow.config \
        -c conf/weblog.disabled.config \
        -params-file params.json \
        -cache false
Nextflow 25.10.4 is available - Please consider updating your version to it

Launching `main.nf` [gloomy_shirley] DSL2 - revision: c8dbf9d8e0

executor >  local (13)
[cd/a09841] process > FASTQC (3)      [100%] 6 of 6 ✔
[71/218fb3] process > TRIM_GALORE (5) [100%] 6 of 6 ✔
[51/85944c] process > MULTIQC         [100%] 1 of 1 ✔

By default the pipeline reads the sample sheet from data/paired-end.csv (see nextflow.config and main.nf). Results are written to results/. Opening results/multiqc/all_paired-end.html would show something like:

docs.title: Deploy to IVCAP
docs.text:
This repository assumes you have the IVCAP CLI installed and configured.

This also requires:

  • an IVCAP service definition file named ivcap-service.yaml, and
  • an IVCAP tool definition file named ivcap-tool.yaml.

Examples of both are provided in this repository:

  • ./ivcap-service.yaml should primarily contain a detailed description of what the pipeline does and the context in which it should be used.
  • Currently, the only other required piece is to ensure controller.pipeline.main_script is set to the Nextflow entrypoint in this repository (i.e. main.nf).
  • ./ivcap-tool.yaml describes the shape of the job request as a JSON schema.
  • The request payload contains both:
    • parameters: the same sort of key/value parameters you would normally put in a Nextflow -params-file, and
    • samples: the sample sheet / sample list describing which read files to process.

docs.title: Actual deployment
docs.text:
The following make target will deploy this pipeline to the IVCAP platform configured as default in the ivcap cli command (ivcap context get)

make deploy

Under the hood this will:

  1. Tar up the pipeline (Nextflow scripts, config, modules, and schema_input.json) into a single file (see make package, producing simple-rna-seq.tar).
  2. Upload that tarball to IVCAP as an artifact (pipeline definition bundle).
  3. Register/update the service identified by SERVICE_ID so it references the uploaded artifact id/URN in the Nextflow controller section of the service definition (see ivcap-service.yaml).

docs.title: More instructions will follow
docs.text: This README is intentionally kept small and focused on the packaging/deployment mechanics. Additional, IVCAP-specific instructions will be added next.

docs.title: IVCAP CLI
docs.text: ivcap is the official command-line interface for interacting with an IVCAP deployment. It can be used directly by humans at a terminal, and is also used by AI agents via its built-in MCP server.

docs.title: What is IVCAP?
docs.text:
IVCAP (Integrated Virtual Collaborative Analysis Platform) is a managed, provenance-aware platform for running, building, and orchestrating analytic services and AI agents. It is designed to help researchers investigate their domains and derive new insights by:

  • collecting, processing and analysing multi-modal and multi-scale data,
  • tracking provenance automatically — recording which service processed which inputs to produce which outputs, and
  • fostering collaboration across disciplines by making data lineage transparent and reproducible.

IVCAP exposes a REST API. This CLI wraps that API into convenient shell commands and also acts as a local MCP server so that AI agents can interact with the platform programmatically.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Each row links to the CLI command that manages that resource.

Concept Description Command Service A packaged, executable capability. Services are registered by developers and invoked by any authorised user. service Job A single execution of a service. Jobs progress through states (pending → executing → succeeded/failed) and emit events. job Artifact Immutable blob-like data (images, JSON, tar'd datasets) produced and consumed by jobs. artifact Collection A named group of artifacts or resources, useful for organising experiment outputs. collection Data Fabric A metadata graph storing aspects — structured records attached to any entity (job, artifact, service, …). Used for provenance and discovery. datafabric Queue An ordered message channel for asynchronous communication between services. queue Secret A named credential stored securely in the platform for use by services at runtime. secret Package A container image in the platform's registry — the execution unit behind a service. package Context A named deployment endpoint and credentials for the CLI to connect to an IVCAP installation. context Nextflow pipeline A Nextflow DSL2 pipeline deployed as an IVCAP service for scalable scientific workflows. nextflow

docs.title: Agent support
docs.text:
Concept Description Command MCP server Exposes all platform operations as Model Context Protocol tools for AI agents. mcp Skill playbook Embedded best-practice workflow guides that agents can read at runtime. skills Agent context Embedded operational guidance (safe defaults, URN conventions, etc.) for AI agents. agent-context

New to IVCAP? See the Getting Started guide for installation, context setup, and your first job.

The complete IVCAP CLI API reference (all classes, methods, and parameters) is available in the dedicated API docs.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide walks you through installing the IVCAP CLI, configuring a deployment context, and verifying your setup.

docs.title: macOS – Homebrew (recommended)
docs.text:
brew tap ivcap-works/ivcap
brew install ivcap

docs.title: macOS / Linux – Download a pre-built binary
docs.text:
1. Visit the Releases page and download the archive for your platform (e.g. ivcap_darwin_arm64.tar.gz).
  2. Extract and move the binary onto your $PATH:
tar xzf ivcap_*.tar.gz
sudo mv ivcap /usr/local/bin/

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: Download the .zip for windows_amd64 from the Releases page, extract ivcap.exe, and add its directory to your PATH.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
Requires Go ≥ 1.21.

git clone https://github.com/ivcap-works/ivcap-cli.git
cd ivcap-cli
make build          # produces ./ivcap
make install        # installs to $GOPATH/bin

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text: ivcap --version

docs.title: 2. Configure a deployment context
docs.text: A context stores the URL of an IVCAP deployment and your credentials so you don't have to repeat them on every command.

docs.title: Create a context
docs.text:
ivcap context create <name> <deployment-url>

Example: 

ivcap context create myivcap https://develop.ivcap.net

Tip

You can have multiple contexts (e.g. develop, staging, prod) and switch between them with ivcap context set <name>.

docs.title: List and switch contexts
docs.text:
ivcap context list          # show all configured contexts
ivcap context set myivcap   # make 'myivcap' the active context
ivcap context get           # show details of the active context

docs.title: 3. Log in
docs.text:
Once a context is active, authenticate to obtain an access token:

ivcap context login

This opens a browser window for your identity provider's login flow. After successful authentication the token is stored locally and refreshed automatically.

docs.title: Headless / non-interactive login (CI, agents)
docs.text:
If you already have a token (e.g. from a CI secret), skip the browser flow:

export IVCAP_ACCESS_TOKEN="<your-token>"

or pass it inline:

ivcap --access-token "<your-token>" service list

docs.title: 4. Verify your connection
docs.text:
ivcap service list --limit 5 --output json

A successful response returns a JSON array of available services. If you see an authentication error, re-run ivcap context login.

docs.title: 5. Submit your first job
docs.text:
# Find a service to run
ivcap service list --limit 10

# Inspect its parameters
ivcap service get urn:ivcap:service:<uuid>

# Create a job (params can be JSON inline or from a file)
ivcap job create urn:ivcap:service:<uuid> \
  --parameter key=value \
  --watch        # stream events until the job finishes

# Retrieve the job result
ivcap job get urn:ivcap:job:<uuid>

docs.title: ivcap artifact create
docs.text: Create a new artifact

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Create a new artifact by uploading file content to IVCAP.

The MIME content-type is auto-detected from the file header when -t/--content-type is omitted. Detection uses the 'mimetype' library (500+ formats) with extension-based overrides for ambiguous types (e.g. .tar.gz → application/x-compressed-tar).

When -t is provided it accepts either a full MIME type or a bare file extension:

-t application/x-compressed-tar full MIME type -t tgz bare extension (same result) -t .tar.gz extension with dot (same result)

Supported extension shorthands include (but are not limited to): Archives: tar, tgz/tar.gz, gz, bz2, xz, zst Earth/env: nc/nc4, fits/fit/fts, hdf5/h5, zarr Bioinformat.: fasta/fa/fna/faa, fastq/fq, bam, sam, vcf, bcf, bed, gff, gff3, gtf Data science: parquet, arrow, mat, npy, npz

When reading from stdin (-f -) the first 512 bytes are sniffed and replayed into the upload stream so no data is lost. For piped tar.gz streams (where the extension is unavailable) pass -t tgz or -t application/x-compressed-tar explicitly.

ivcap artifact create [flags] -n name -f file|-

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
--chunk-size int        Chunk size for splitting large files (default 10000000)
  -c, --collection string     Assigns artifact to a specific collection
  -t, --content-type string   Content type of artifact; auto-detected when omitted. Accepts a full MIME type (e.g. application/x-compressed-tar) or a bare extension (e.g. tgz, nc, fasta)
  -f, --file string           Path to file containing artifact content

docs.title: ivcap collection add
docs.text: Add item(s) to an existing collection

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Add one or more items to an existing collection.

Items can be specified in two ways (both may be combined):

  1. As positional URN arguments after the collection URN.
  2. Via --dir: a directory path or glob pattern. Each matching file is uploaded as an artifact (skipped if already uploaded) and the resulting artifact URN is used as the item.

A 'collection-item' aspect (urn:ivcap:schema:collection-item.1) is created for each new item. Duplicates (same collection + item) are detected and skipped.

ivcap collection add collectionURN [urn...] [--dir <dir-or-glob>] [flags]

--dir string   Directory or glob pattern of files to upload and add

docs.title: ivcap mcp
docs.text: Start an MCP server for accessing all tools on an IVCAP platform

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Start an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server.

In addition to MCP Tools for calling platform services, this server also exposes the ivcap-cli release's embedded agent skills via MCP Resources and Prompts ("MCP-Provisioned Skills").

Resources (preferred if your MCP client exposes resources/read to LLMs): - skills://manifest JSON manifest of available skills - skills://catalog.json JSON catalog (metadata + hashes; no bodies) - skills://CONTEXT.md General agent best-practices for ivcap-cli - skills://SKILLS.md Top-level skills tree index - skills://{name}/SKILL.md Skill playbook body (markdown) - skills://file/{path} Any embedded markdown file (e.g. category SKILLS.md)

Bridge Tools (fallback for clients that don't expose resources/read): - list_skills List available skill playbooks (same as skills://manifest) - read_skill Read a skill playbook by name (same as skills://{name}/SKILL.md)

Prompts: - use-ivcap-best-practices Instructs an agent to load CONTEXT + relevant skills (prefers resources/read, falls back to tools if needed)

Note: Many MCP clients (including Claude Desktop) don't currently expose resources/read to LLMs for programmatic access. The bridge tools provide equivalent functionality via tools/call until client support improves.

Recommended MCP client system prompt:

Before answering any task: 1. Call resources/list on all connected MCP servers (if available) 2. Identify resources matching: SKILL.md, instructions, prompt* 3. Fetch and read matching resources via resources/read (if available) 4. Otherwise use list_skills and read_skill tools 5. Apply those instructions when completing the user's request

ivcap mcp [flags]

      --port int             optional port to open for SSE connection to MCP server (default -1)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: ivcap is the official command-line interface for interacting with an IVCAP deployment. It can be used directly by humans at a terminal, and is also used by AI agents via its built-in MCP server.

docs.title: What is IVCAP?
docs.text:
IVCAP (Integrated Virtual Collaborative Analysis Platform) is a managed, provenance-aware platform for running, building, and orchestrating analytic services and AI agents. It is designed to help researchers investigate their domains and derive new insights by:

  • collecting, processing and analysing multi-modal and multi-scale data,
  • tracking provenance automatically — recording which service processed which inputs to produce which outputs, and
  • fostering collaboration across disciplines by making data lineage transparent and reproducible.

IVCAP exposes a REST API. This CLI wraps that API into convenient shell commands and also acts as a local MCP server so that AI agents can interact with the platform programmatically.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: Concept Description Service A packaged, executable capability (think "function endpoint with configuration"). Services are registered by developers and can be invoked by any authorised user. Job A single execution of a service with a specific set of inputs. Jobs progress through states (pending → executing → succeeded/failed) and emit events. Artifact Immutable blob-like data referenced by URN (images, JSON files, tar'd datasets, …). Artifacts are produced and consumed by jobs. Data Fabric A metadata graph that stores aspects — structured records attached to any entity (artifact, job, service, …). Used for provenance, annotation, and discovery. Aspect A single structured record in the Data Fabric, described by a schema URN. IVCAP writes provenance aspects automatically; users can write their own. Queue An ordered message channel for asynchronous communication between services. Secret A named credential stored securely in the platform for use by services at runtime. Package A Docker container image stored in the platform's registry — the execution unit behind a service. Collection A named group of artifacts or other resources, useful for organising experiment outputs.

docs.title: What you can do with this CLI
Manage the platform from the command line
docs.text:
# Set up a deployment context
ivcap context create my-deployment https://my.ivcap.net
ivcap context login

# Discover services
ivcap service list
ivcap service get urn:ivcap:service:…

# Submit and monitor jobs
ivcap job create urn:ivcap:service:… -f params.json --watch

# Work with artifacts
ivcap artifact list
ivcap artifact get urn:ivcap:artifact:…
ivcap artifact download urn:ivcap:artifact:… -f output.bin

# Query the Data Fabric
ivcap datafabric query --entity urn:ivcap:artifact:…

docs.title: Run Nextflow pipelines
docs.text:
The nextflow subcommand provides higher-level wrappers for deploying and running Nextflow-based pipeline services:

ivcap nextflow create ./my-pipeline.tar.gz
ivcap nextflow run urn:ivcap:service:… -f params.json --watch
ivcap nextflow job-view urn:ivcap:job:…   # open execution report in browser

docs.title: Agent / MCP usage
docs.text:
ivcap mcp starts a local Model Context Protocol server that exposes all platform operations as MCP tools. AI agents (Claude, GPT, LangChain, …) connect to this server and can submit jobs, download results, query provenance, and build multi-step pipelines — all without writing custom API code.

# Start the MCP server (STDIO mode — used by most agent frameworks)
ivcap mcp

# Start the MCP server in SSE mode
ivcap mcp --port 8088

The server also exposes embedded skill playbooks as MCP Resources so that agents can discover best practices and workflow patterns at runtime:

ivcap skills list
ivcap skills show ivcap-job-create

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Pre-built binaries are available for macOS, Linux, and Windows at the GitHub releases page.

macOS (Homebrew): 

brew tap ivcap-works/ivcap
brew install ivcap

From source: 

git clone https://github.com/ivcap-works/ivcap-cli.git
cd ivcap-cli
make build
make install

docs.text:
# 1. Create a context for your IVCAP deployment
ivcap context create mydeployment https://your.ivcap.net

# 2. Log in
ivcap context login

# 3. List available services
ivcap service list --limit 10

# 4. Submit a job
ivcap job create urn:ivcap:service:<uuid> -f job-params.json --watch

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The IVCAP API uses Bearer token authentication. The SDK accepts a JWT token and injects it automatically into every request.

docs.title: Option 1 – Configuration Object (recommended for production)
docs.text:
import { IvcapClient } from "@ivcap/client";

const client = new IvcapClient({
  baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",
  token: "eyJhbGciOiJ...",
});

docs.title: Option 2 – Environment Variables
docs.text:
If no token is provided in the config, the SDK automatically reads:

Variable Description IVCAP_URL Base URL of your IVCAP deployment IVCAP_JWT Bearer token 
export IVCAP_URL=https://develop.ivcap.net
export IVCAP_JWT=eyJhbGciOiJ...

// Picks up IVCAP_URL and IVCAP_JWT automatically
const client = new IvcapClient();

docs.title: Option 3 – .env File (development only)
docs.text:
# .env
IVCAP_URL=https://develop.ivcap.net
IVCAP_JWT=eyJhbGciOiJ...

import "dotenv/config"; // loads .env before importing the client
import { IvcapClient } from "@ivcap/client";

const client = new IvcapClient();

Security warning

Never commit .env files or hard-coded tokens to version control. Add .env to your .gitignore.

docs.title: Obtaining a Token
docs.text:
Tokens are obtained from the IVCAP identity provider. Use the ivcap CLI:

ivcap context login
ivcap context get access-token

Copy the output and set it as IVCAP_JWT.

docs.title: Token Rotation at Runtime
docs.text:
For long-running processes (agents, background workers), you may need to refresh the token without restarting the client:

const client = new IvcapClient({ baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net" });

// Rotate the token every 55 minutes
setInterval(async () => {
  const newToken = await myTokenProvider.refresh();
  client.setToken(newToken);
}, 55 * 60 * 1_000);

See client.setToken() for details.

docs.title: Authentication Errors
docs.text:
If your token is missing or expired, the SDK throws an UnauthorizedError:

import { IvcapClient, UnauthorizedError } from "@ivcap/client";

try {
  const svc = await client.services.get("urn:ivcap:service:abc...");
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof UnauthorizedError) {
    console.error("Token missing or expired — please log in again.");
  }
}

docs.title: Using Multiple Deployments
docs.text:
Create separate client instances for each deployment:

const devClient  = new IvcapClient({ baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",    token: devToken });
const prodClient = new IvcapClient({ baseUrl: "https://production.ivcap.net", token: prodToken });

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide walks you through your first complete IVCAP workflow in TypeScript: discover a service, upload data, run a job, and download the results.

docs.title: 1. Install the SDK
docs.text: npm install @ivcap/client

docs.title: 2. Create a Client
docs.text:
import { IvcapClient } from "@ivcap/client";

const client = new IvcapClient({
  baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",
  token: process.env.IVCAP_JWT,
});

Or rely on environment variables (IVCAP_URL and IVCAP_JWT):

const client = new IvcapClient(); // reads env vars automatically

docs.title: 3. Browse Available Services
docs.text:
// Iterate all services (lazy pagination)
for await (const svc of client.services.list()) {
  console.log(svc.id, svc.name);
}

// Fetch details about a specific service
const svc = await client.services.get("urn:ivcap:service:abc-123");
console.log(svc.description);
svc.parameters.forEach(p => {
  console.log(`  ${p.name} (${p.type})${p.optional ? " [optional]" : ""}`);
});

docs.title: 4. Upload an Input Artifact
docs.text:
const artifact = await client.artifacts.upload(
  JSON.stringify({ temperature: [21.3, 22.1, 19.8] }),
  { name: "sensor-data.json", contentType: "application/json" }
);
console.log("Uploaded artifact:", artifact.id);

You can also upload a file in Node.js:

import { createReadStream } from "fs";

const artifact = await client.artifacts.upload(
  createReadStream("data.csv"),
  { name: "data.csv", contentType: "text/csv" }
);

docs.title: 5. Submit a Job and Wait for Results
docs.text:
const job = await client.jobs.createAndWait(
  "urn:ivcap:service:my-analysis-service",
  {
    parameters: [
      { name: "input",     value: artifact.id },
      { name: "threshold", value: "0.05" },
    ],
    name: "My first job",
  },
  {
    pollInterval: 5_000,   // check every 5 seconds
    timeout:     300_000,  // give up after 5 minutes
    onUpdate: (j) => console.log("status:", j.status),
  }
);

console.log("Final status:", job.status);

docs.title: 6. Download the Results
docs.text:
if (job.status === "succeeded") {
  for (const product of job.products.items) {
    console.log("Product:", product.id, product.mimeType);

    // Download as text
    const text = await client.artifacts.downloadText(product.id);
    console.log(text);

    // Or download as parsed JSON
    const obj = await client.artifacts.downloadJson(product.id);
    console.log(obj);
  }
} else {
  console.error("Job did not succeed:", job.status);
}

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
import { IvcapClient, JobResource } from "@ivcap/client";

async function main() {
  const client = new IvcapClient({
    baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",
    token: process.env.IVCAP_JWT,
  });

  // 1. Find the service
  const serviceId = "urn:ivcap:service:my-analysis-service";
  const svc = await client.services.get(serviceId);
  console.log("Using service:", svc.name);

  // 2. Upload input data
  const artifact = await client.artifacts.upload(
    JSON.stringify({ values: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] }),
    { name: "input.json", contentType: "application/json" }
  );

  // 3. Submit & wait
  const job = await client.jobs.createAndWait(
    serviceId,
    {
      parameters: JobResource.buildParameters({
        input:     artifact.id,
        threshold: "0.5",
      }),
      name: "Quick-start run",
    },
    { onUpdate: (j) => console.log("  →", j.status) }
  );

  // 4. Download results
  if (job.status === "succeeded") {
    for (const p of job.products.items) {
      const result = await client.artifacts.downloadJson(p.id);
      console.log("Result:", result);
    }
  }
}

main().catch(console.error);

docs.title: Advanced Usage
docs.text: This guide covers less common but important patterns: token rotation, low-level HTTP access, browser integration, and working with queues and secrets.

docs.title: Token Rotation
docs.text:
For long-running processes (background workers, agents, servers), your JWT token may expire while the client is running. Rotate it without restarting:

import { IvcapClient } from "@ivcap/client";

const client = new IvcapClient({
  baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",
  token: await getInitialToken(),
});

// Rotate every 55 minutes (before the 1-hour expiry)
setInterval(async () => {
  const newToken = await myTokenProvider.refresh();
  client.setToken(newToken);
  console.log("Token rotated at", new Date().toISOString());
}, 55 * 60 * 1_000);

docs.title: Low-level HTTP Access
docs.text:
For endpoints not yet covered by the SDK, access the underlying Axios instance directly:

const axios = client.getHttpClient().getAxios();

// Custom GET request
const response = await axios.get("/1/some/custom/endpoint");
console.log(response.data);

// POST with a custom body
await axios.post("/1/custom/resource", { myField: "value" });

Note

Prefer the typed resource methods (client.artifacts, client.jobs, …) whenever they cover your use case. Fall back to the raw Axios instance only for non-standard or experimental endpoints.

docs.title: Custom Request Headers
docs.text:
Pass custom headers to every request via the config:

const client = new IvcapClient({
  baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",
  token:   process.env.IVCAP_JWT,
  headers: {
    "X-Trace-Id":  "my-trace-12345",
    "X-Client-Id": "my-service",
  },
});

docs.title: Request Timeout
docs.text:
The default timeout is 30 seconds. Override it globally:

const client = new IvcapClient({
  baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",
  token:   process.env.IVCAP_JWT,
  timeout: 60_000,  // 60 seconds
});

docs.title: Working with Queues
docs.text:
Queues allow services and external systems to communicate asynchronously.

// Create a queue
const queue = await client.queues.create({
  name:        "results-queue",
  description: "Receives job completion events",
});

// Publish a message
await client.queues.enqueue(queue.id, {
  schema:  "urn:example:schema:event:job-done:1",
  content: { jobId: "urn:ivcap:job:...", status: "succeeded" },
});

// Consume messages in a loop
while (true) {
  const msg = await client.queues.dequeue(queue.id);
  if (msg === null) break; // queue is empty

  console.log(msg.schema, msg.content);
}

// Clean up
await client.queues.delete(queue.id);

docs.title: Working with Secrets
docs.text:
Store credentials securely on the platform:

// Store a secret
await client.secrets.set({
  secretName:  "MY_API_KEY",
  secretValue: "super-secret-value",
  expiryTime:  Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 86_400, // 24h from now (Unix seconds)
});

// List secrets (names + expiry only — values are NOT returned)
const list = await client.secrets.list();
list.forEach(s => console.log(s.secretName, s.expiryTime));

// Retrieve a secret value
const secret = await client.secrets.get("MY_API_KEY");
console.log(secret.secretValue);

// Delete
await client.secrets.delete("MY_API_KEY");

docs.title: Working with Projects
docs.text:
// List all projects
for await (const p of client.projects.list()) {
  console.log(p.urn, p.name, p.status);
}

// Get project details
const proj = await client.projects.get("urn:ivcap:project:abc...");
console.log(proj.properties);

// Create a new project
const newProj = await client.projects.create({
  name: "Fire Risk Analysis 2026",
  properties: { region: "Tasmania" },
});

docs.title: Browser / Vite / Next.js Usage
docs.text:
The SDK ships both ESM and CJS builds with no Node-specific APIs in the core logic. Axios handles HTTP and works transparently in browser environments.

// Works in Vite, Create React App, Next.js client components, etc.
import { IvcapClient } from "@ivcap/client";

const client = new IvcapClient({
  baseUrl: import.meta.env.VITE_IVCAP_URL,
  token:   import.meta.env.VITE_IVCAP_JWT,
});

Don't expose tokens to browsers in production

If you use the SDK in the browser, ensure tokens are obtained via your own backend (e.g., a Next.js API route) and not hard-coded in the frontend bundle.

docs.title: Using Multiple Clients
docs.text:
Create separate instances for different deployments or service accounts:

const devClient  = new IvcapClient({ baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",    token: devToken });
const prodClient = new IvcapClient({ baseUrl: "https://production.ivcap.net", token: prodToken });

docs.title: Working with Artifacts
docs.text: Artifacts are binary or structured data blobs stored on IVCAP — sensor readings, images, CSV files, trained models, or any other data. They are the primary input/output mechanism for services.

docs.title: Upload a String or JSON
docs.text:
const artifact = await client.artifacts.upload(
  JSON.stringify({ temperature: [21.3, 22.1, 19.8] }),
  { name: "sensor-data.json", contentType: "application/json" }
);
console.log("Created:", artifact.id, artifact.status);

docs.title: Upload a Buffer or ArrayBuffer
docs.text:
const buffer = Buffer.from("Hello, IVCAP!");

const artifact = await client.artifacts.upload(buffer, {
  name:        "hello.txt",
  contentType: "text/plain",
});

docs.title: Upload a File (Node.js)
docs.text:
import { createReadStream } from "fs";
import { readFile } from "fs/promises";

// Stream (memory-efficient for large files)
const artifact = await client.artifacts.upload(
  createReadStream("large-dataset.csv"),
  { name: "large-dataset.csv", contentType: "text/csv" }
);

// Buffer (simpler for small files)
const bytes = await readFile("image.png");
const img = await client.artifacts.upload(bytes, {
  name:        "image.png",
  contentType: "image/png",
});

docs.title: Upload a Blob (Browser)
docs.text:
const file = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#file")!.files![0];
const artifact = await client.artifacts.upload(file, {
  name:        file.name,
  contentType: file.type,
});

docs.title: Upload Options
docs.text: Option Type Description name string Human-friendly name for the artifact contentType string MIME type (e.g. application/json, image/png) collection URN Assign the artifact to a named collection policy URN Access policy URN

docs.title: Download as ArrayBuffer
docs.text:
const bytes: ArrayBuffer = await client.artifacts.download("urn:ivcap:artifact:abc...");
// write to disk, process as binary, etc.

docs.title: Download as UTF-8 String
docs.text:
const text = await client.artifacts.downloadText("urn:ivcap:artifact:abc...");
console.log(text);

docs.title: Download and Parse as JSON
docs.text:
interface MyResult {
  score: number;
  label: string;
}

const result = await client.artifacts.downloadJson<MyResult>("urn:ivcap:artifact:abc...");
console.log(result.score, result.label);

docs.title: Listing Artifacts
docs.text:
// Iterate all artifacts (lazy pagination)
for await (const a of client.artifacts.list()) {
  console.log(a.id, a.name, a.status, a.mimeType);
}

// With options
for await (const a of client.artifacts.list({
  limit:     50,
  orderBy:   "name",
  orderDesc: false,
})) {
  console.log(a.name);
}

docs.title: Getting Artifact Metadata
docs.text:
const detail = await client.artifacts.get("urn:ivcap:artifact:abc...");

console.log(detail.id);
console.log(detail.name);
console.log(detail.status);       // "pending" | "partial" | "ready" | "error" | "unknown"
console.log(detail.mimeType);
console.log(detail.size);         // bytes
console.log(detail.createdAt);
console.log(detail.lastModifiedAt);
console.log(detail.dataHref);     // direct download URL (if available)

docs.title: Artifact Status Values
docs.text: Status Meaning pending Upload has started but not completed partial Partially uploaded (large multipart upload) ready Fully uploaded and available for download error Upload failed unknown Status could not be determined

docs.title: Job Products
docs.text:
When a job succeeds, its output artifacts are listed under job.products.items:

const job = await client.jobs.createAndWait(serviceId, req);

if (job.status === "succeeded") {
  for (const product of job.products.items) {
    console.log(product.id, product.mimeType, product.size);

    const result = await client.artifacts.downloadJson(product.id);
    console.log(result);
  }
}

Each ProductListItem has: id, status, href, dataHref, name, mimeType, size.

docs.title: The Datafabric & Aspects
docs.text: Aspects are typed, time-stamped JSON metadata records attached to any IVCAP entity. They form the foundation of IVCAP's Datafabric — an emergent knowledge graph that records provenance, annotations, and relationships across all platform resources.

docs.title: What is an Aspect?
docs.text:
Every aspect has:

  • An entity — the thing it describes (any URN: artifact, job, service, …)
  • A schema — a URN identifying the type of metadata
  • Content — an arbitrary JSON payload conforming to the schema
  • A validity period — when it was asserted (validFrom) and optionally retracted (validTo)

Aspects are immutable in the sense that they are never edited in-place — they are retracted (given an end time) and replaced by a new assertion. This gives you a complete audit trail and enables historical ("time-travel") queries.

docs.title: Creating an Aspect
docs.text:
const aspect = await client.aspects.create({
  entity:  "urn:ivcap:artifact:abc-123",
  schema:  "urn:example:schema:label:1",
  content: { label: "high-quality", confidence: 0.98 },
});

console.log(aspect.id, aspect.validFrom);

docs.title: All Aspects for an Entity
docs.text:
for await (const a of client.aspects.list({
  entity: "urn:ivcap:artifact:abc-123",
})) {
  console.log(a.schema, a.validFrom, a.content);
}

docs.title: Filtered by Schema
docs.text:
for await (const a of client.aspects.list({
  entity: artifactId,
  schema: "urn:example:schema:label:1",
})) {
  console.log(a.content);
}

docs.title: Include Content in the List Response
docs.text:
By default, list() omits the content field for performance. Set includeContent: true to include it without a separate get() call:

for await (const a of client.aspects.list({
  entity:         artifactId,
  includeContent: true,
})) {
  console.log(a.schema, a.content); // content is populated
}

docs.title: Historical Query (Time Travel)
docs.text:
Query metadata as it existed at a specific point in time:

const historical = await client.aspects.list({
  entity: artifactId,
  atTime: "2025-06-01T12:00:00Z",
}).toArray();

docs.title: Getting a Single Aspect
docs.text:
const aspect = await client.aspects.get("urn:ivcap:aspect:abc...");

console.log(aspect.entity);
console.log(aspect.schema);
console.log(aspect.content);
console.log(aspect.asserter);  // who created this aspect
console.log(aspect.validFrom);
console.log(aspect.validTo);   // undefined if still active

docs.title: Updating an Aspect
docs.text:
update() retracts the existing aspect and creates a replacement:

await client.aspects.update("urn:ivcap:aspect:abc...", {
  label:      "revised-quality",
  confidence: 0.75,
});

docs.title: Retracting an Aspect
docs.text:
Retract (logically delete) an aspect — it becomes inactive but is never removed:

await client.aspects.retract("urn:ivcap:aspect:abc...");

docs.title: Provenance Queries
docs.text:
IVCAP automatically records relationships between jobs, inputs, and outputs as aspects. You can query them:

// What jobs produced a given artifact?
for await (const a of client.aspects.list({
  entity: artifactId,
  schema: "urn:ivcap:schema:artifact-usedBy-order.1",
})) {
  console.log("Produced by job:", a.content);
}

// What artifacts did a job consume?
for await (const a of client.aspects.list({
  entity: jobId,
  schema: "urn:ivcap:schema:order-usedArtifact.1",
})) {
  console.log("Input artifact:", a.content);
}

docs.title: AspectListOptions
docs.text: Option Type Description entity URN Filter by entity URN schema string Filter by schema URN prefix contentPath string JSON-path filter on the content field atTime DateTimeString Historical query — aspects valid at this time includeContent boolean Include content in list response (default: false) limit number Max items per page orderBy string Sort field orderDirection "ASC" \| "DESC" Sort direction

docs.title: Collections Guide
docs.text:
Collections are a first-class concept in the IVCAP TypeScript SDK that let you group any mix of IVCAP entities (artifacts, jobs, other collections, …) under a single named handle.

Virtual resource

Collections are not a native IVCAP API endpoint. They are implemented entirely on top of the DataFabric aspect store (/1/aspects). Two aspect schemas are used; no other API surface is required.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
erDiagram
    COLLECTION {
        URN id "urn:ivcap:collection:<uuid>"
        URN aspectId "underlying aspect URN"
        string name
        string description
        DateTimeString createdAt
    }
    COLLECTION_ITEM {
        URN id "collection-item aspect URN"
        URN entity "the member entity URN"
        DateTimeString addedAt
    }
    COLLECTION ||--o{ COLLECTION_ITEM : "has members"

docs.title: Aspect schemas
docs.text:
Schema URN Attached to Content fields urn:ivcap:schema:collection.1 urn:ivcap:collection:<uuid> name, description? urn:ivcap:schema:collection-item.1 urn:ivcap:collection:<uuid> entity

Both aspects are asserted on the collection entity — the membership record content.entity field holds the URN of the item that was added.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import { IvcapClient } from "@ivcap/client";

const client = new IvcapClient({
  baseUrl: "https://develop.ivcap.net",
  token: process.env.IVCAP_JWT,
});

// 1. Create a collection
const col = await client.collections.create({
  name: "My curated dataset",
  description: "Artifacts selected for model training v2",
});
console.log(col.id); // urn:ivcap:collection:<uuid>

// 2. Add items
await client.collections.addItem(col.id, "urn:ivcap:artifact:...");
await client.collections.addItem(col.id, "urn:ivcap:artifact:...");

// 3. List all items
for await (const item of client.collections.listItems(col.id)) {
  console.log(item.entity, item.addedAt);
}

// 4. Remove one item
await client.collections.removeItem(col.id, "urn:ivcap:artifact:...");

// 5. Retract the entire collection (header + all memberships)
await client.collections.retract(col.id);

docs.title: create(input)
docs.text:
Creates a new, empty collection.

const col = await client.collections.create({
  name: "Training set A",
  description: "Optional free-text description",
  policy: "urn:ivcap:policy:...", // optional
});

How it works:

  1. A synthetic entity URN urn:ivcap:collection:<uuid> is generated client-side using crypto.randomUUID().
  2. A POST /1/aspects request asserts a collection.1 aspect on that entity.
  3. The returned CollectionListItem maps the response fields.
sequenceDiagram
    participant SDK
    participant API as IVCAP API
    SDK->>SDK: entityId = urn:ivcap:collection:<uuid>
    SDK->>API: POST /1/aspects<br/>{entity, schema: collection.1, content: {name, description}}
    API-->>SDK: AspectDetail {id, entity, validFrom, content}
    SDK-->>SDK: return CollectionListItem

docs.title: get(id)
docs.text:
Fetches a collection by its entity URN.

const col = await client.collections.get("urn:ivcap:collection:...");
console.log(col.name, col.createdAt);

Throws NotFoundError when no matching collection exists.

sequenceDiagram
    participant SDK
    participant API as IVCAP API
    SDK->>API: GET /1/aspects?entity=<id>&schema=collection.1&include-content=true&limit=1
    API-->>SDK: {items: [...], links: [...]}
    alt items is empty
        SDK-->>SDK: throw NotFoundError
    else found
        SDK-->>SDK: return CollectionListItem
    end

docs.title: list(options?)
docs.text:
Returns an async iterator over all collections visible to the caller.

for await (const col of client.collections.list({ limit: 20 })) {
  console.log(col.id, col.name);
}

// Or collect everything into an array
const all = await client.collections.list().toArray();

Options:

Option Type Description limit number Maximum items per page atTime DateTimeString Point-in-time query

docs.title: addItem(collectionId, itemId, options?)
docs.text:
Adds an entity to a collection. The operation is idempotent — calling it twice with the same (collectionId, itemId) pair returns the existing membership record without creating a duplicate.

const membership = await client.collections.addItem(
  col.id,
  "urn:ivcap:artifact:abc...",
);
console.log(membership.id);      // aspect URN of the membership record
console.log(membership.entity);  // urn:ivcap:artifact:abc...
console.log(membership.addedAt); // ISO-8601 timestamp

Dedup / idempotency contract:

  1. A GET /1/aspects request with a content-path JSONPath filter ($.entity == "<itemId>") checks whether a matching membership already exists.
  2. If found → return the existing record; no POST is issued.
  3. If not found → issue POST /1/aspects with a collection-item.1 aspect.
  4. If the dedup GET itself fails (including any 5xx error) → fall through and unconditionally POST. This ensures forward progress even under transient API failures.
sequenceDiagram
    participant SDK
    participant API as IVCAP API
    SDK->>API: GET /1/aspects?entity=<collectionId>&schema=collection-item.1<br/>&content-path=$.entity=="<itemId>"&include-content=true&limit=1
    alt found existing record
        API-->>SDK: {items: [existing], ...}
        SDK-->>SDK: return existing CollectionItem (no POST)
    else not found
        API-->>SDK: {items: [], ...}
        SDK->>API: POST /1/aspects<br/>{entity: collectionId, schema: collection-item.1, content: {entity: itemId}}
        API-->>SDK: AspectDetail
        SDK-->>SDK: return new CollectionItem
    else GET threw error (5xx)
        SDK->>API: POST /1/aspects (fall-through)
        API-->>SDK: AspectDetail
        SDK-->>SDK: return new CollectionItem
    end

docs.title: removeItem(collectionId, itemId)
docs.text:
Removes an entity from a collection. No-op if the entity is not a member.

await client.collections.removeItem(col.id, "urn:ivcap:artifact:abc...");

sequenceDiagram
    participant SDK
    participant API as IVCAP API
    SDK->>API: GET /1/aspects (dedup check — find item aspect)
    alt item aspect found
        SDK->>API: DELETE /1/aspects/<aspectId>
    else not found or error
        SDK-->>SDK: return (no-op)
    end

docs.title: listItems(collectionId, options?)
docs.text:
Returns an async iterator over all members of a collection.

for await (const item of client.collections.listItems(col.id)) {
  console.log(item.entity);
}

// Collect into an array
const members = await client.collections.listItems(col.id).toArray();

Options mirror those of list().

docs.title: retract(id)
docs.text:
Retracts a collection and all of its membership records.

await client.collections.retract(col.id);

Order of operations:

  1. listItems(id).toArray() — fetches all membership aspects.
  2. DELETE /1/aspects/<itemAspectId> for every membership, executed in parallel via Promise.all.
  3. get(id) — fetches the collection header aspect.
  4. DELETE /1/aspects/<headerAspectId> — retracts the collection header.

Throws NotFoundError if the collection does not exist (step 3 fails with no items).

sequenceDiagram
    participant SDK
    participant API as IVCAP API
    SDK->>API: GET /1/aspects?entity=<id>&schema=collection-item.1 (all items)
    loop for each membership aspect (parallel)
        SDK->>API: DELETE /1/aspects/<itemAspectId>
    end
    SDK->>API: GET /1/aspects?entity=<id>&schema=collection.1 (header)
    SDK->>API: DELETE /1/aspects/<headerAspectId>

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
All list operations return a PageIterator<T> which supports:

// Async for-of (recommended — streams lazily)
for await (const col of client.collections.list()) { … }

// Collect all pages into an array
const all = await client.collections.list().toArray();

// Fetch the first page only
const first = await client.collections.list().firstPage();

// Callback style
await client.collections.listItems(col.id).forEach(async (item) => {
  await process(item);
});

The page cursor is extracted from the links[rel=next].href field of each response and passed as the page query parameter on the next request.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Situation Thrown error get or retract on a non-existent collection NotFoundError addItem dedup GET returns 5xx Falls through to POST (no error thrown) removeItem when item is not a member Silently returns (no-op) removeItem when lookup GET throws Silently returns (no-op) Any other network / authentication error Propagated to caller

All errors are instances of IvcapError (or a subclass) with a .statusCode property. See the Error Handling guide for details.

docs.title: TypeScript Types
docs.text:
import type {
  CollectionListItem,
  CollectionItem,
  CreateCollectionRequest,
  CollectionListOptions,
} from "@ivcap/client";

// CollectionListItem – returned by create / get / list
interface CollectionListItem {
  id: URN;           // urn:ivcap:collection:<uuid>
  aspectId: URN;     // underlying DataFabric aspect URN
  name: string;
  description?: string;
  createdAt: DateTimeString;
}

// CollectionItem – returned by addItem / listItems
interface CollectionItem {
  id: URN;           // collection-item aspect URN (used by removeItem internally)
  entity: URN;       // the member entity URN
  addedAt: DateTimeString;
}

// CreateCollectionRequest – input for create
interface CreateCollectionRequest {
  name: string;
  description?: string;
  policy?: URN;      // optional access policy
}

// CollectionListOptions – pagination / filtering for list / listItems
interface CollectionListOptions {
  limit?: number;
  page?: string;
  atTime?: DateTimeString;
}

docs.title: Key Invariants
docs.text:
The following invariants hold for any correct implementation:

  1. Every collection has exactly one collection.1 aspect, identified by its entity URN.
  2. The entity URN of a collection always matches /^urn:ivcap:collection:[0-9a-f-]{36}$/.
  3. create never re-uses an existing entity URN; each call generates a fresh UUID.
  4. addItem called twice with the same arguments is idempotent — only one collection-item.1 aspect is asserted.
  5. addItem succeeds even when the dedup GET fails with a 5xx error.
  6. removeItem called on a non-member is a no-op (no DELETE is issued).
  7. listItems returns only collection-item.1 aspects attached to the given collection entity.
  8. retract retracts membership aspects before the collection header.
  9. retract on an empty collection still retracts the header.
  10. retract throws NotFoundError when the collection does not exist.
  11. get throws NotFoundError when the collection does not exist.
  12. All list operations support cursor-based pagination via the page option.

Full API Reference

The complete JavaScript/TypeScript Client SDK API reference (all classes, methods, and parameters) is available in the dedicated API docs.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The IVCAP SDK throws typed error classes that map directly to HTTP status codes. This makes it easy to write robust, specific error handlers.

docs.title: Error Class Hierarchy
docs.text:
Error
└── IvcapError          (base class — all IVCAP errors)
    ├── BadRequestError          (HTTP 400)
    ├── UnauthorizedError        (HTTP 401)
    ├── ForbiddenError           (HTTP 403)
    ├── NotFoundError            (HTTP 404)
    ├── ConflictError            (HTTP 409)
    ├── InvalidParameterError    (HTTP 422)
    ├── NotImplementedError      (HTTP 501)
    ├── ServiceUnavailableError  (HTTP 503)
    ├── AmbiguousResultError     (multiple matches where one expected)
    └── TimeoutError             (polling timeout — no HTTP code)

docs.title: Catching a Specific Error Type
docs.text:
import {
  IvcapClient,
  NotFoundError,
  UnauthorizedError,
  TimeoutError,
  ForbiddenError,
} from "@ivcap/client";

try {
  const job = await client.jobs.get(serviceId, "urn:ivcap:job:unknown");
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof NotFoundError) {
    console.error("Job not found:", err.resourceId);
  } else if (err instanceof UnauthorizedError) {
    console.error("Token missing or expired — please log in again");
  } else if (err instanceof ForbiddenError) {
    console.error("Insufficient permissions:", err.message);
  } else if (err instanceof TimeoutError) {
    console.error("Polling timed out:", err.message);
  } else {
    throw err; // re-throw unknown errors
  }
}

docs.title: Catching Any IVCAP Error
docs.text:
import { IvcapError } from "@ivcap/client";

try {
  await client.artifacts.upload(data, opts);
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof IvcapError) {
    console.error(`IVCAP error [${err.statusCode}]: ${err.message}`);
    console.error("Details:", err.details);
  } else {
    throw err;
  }
}

docs.title: IvcapError (base class)
docs.text:
All IVCAP errors extend this class.

Property Type Description message string Human-readable error description statusCode number \| undefined HTTP status code (if applicable) details unknown Raw response body for debugging

docs.title: BadRequestError (400)
docs.text:
The request was malformed — check your parameters.

import { BadRequestError } from "@ivcap/client";
// err.message — what was wrong
// err.details — the full server response

docs.title: UnauthorizedError (401)
docs.text:
The token is missing, expired, or invalid.

import { UnauthorizedError } from "@ivcap/client";
// err.message — "Not authorized" or server message

docs.title: ForbiddenError (403)
docs.text:
You are authenticated, but lack permission for this resource.

import { ForbiddenError } from "@ivcap/client";
// err.message, err.details

docs.title: NotFoundError (404)
docs.text:
The requested resource does not exist.

import { NotFoundError } from "@ivcap/client";
// err.resourceId — the URN that wasn't found (if returned by the server)

docs.title: ConflictError (409)
docs.text:
A resource with the same identity already exists.

import { ConflictError } from "@ivcap/client";
// err.resourceId — the conflicting resource URN

docs.title: InvalidParameterError (422)
docs.text:
A parameter value failed server-side validation.

import { InvalidParameterError } from "@ivcap/client";
// err.paramName  — which parameter was invalid
// err.paramValue — the value that was rejected

docs.title: ServiceUnavailableError (503)
docs.text:
The platform is temporarily unavailable. Implement retry with back-off.

import { ServiceUnavailableError } from "@ivcap/client";

docs.title: TimeoutError (polling timeout)
docs.text:
Thrown by jobs.createAndWait() or jobs.waitUntilDone() when the job doesn't complete within the configured timeout window.

import { TimeoutError } from "@ivcap/client";

try {
  const job = await client.jobs.createAndWait(serviceId, req, {
    timeout: 30_000,  // 30 seconds
  });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof TimeoutError) {
    console.error("Increase timeout or check service health");
  }
}

docs.title: Simple Retry with Back-off
docs.text:
async function withRetry<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  maxAttempts = 3,
  delayMs = 1_000,
): Promise<T> {
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (err) {
      if (attempt === maxAttempts) throw err;
      if (err instanceof ServiceUnavailableError) {
        const wait = delayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1);
        console.warn(`Attempt ${attempt} failed — retrying in ${wait}ms…`);
        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, wait));
      } else {
        throw err; // don't retry non-transient errors
      }
    }
  }
  throw new Error("unreachable");
}

// Usage
const artifact = await withRetry(() =>
  client.artifacts.upload(data, opts)
);

docs.title: Running Jobs
docs.text:
A job is a single execution of an IVCAP service.

No top-level /jobs endpoint

IVCAP exposes jobs through two API layers the SDK stitches together automatically. See the architecture note in the API reference for details.

docs.title: Job Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> scheduled : create()
    scheduled --> executing : execution starts
    executing --> succeeded : completed successfully
    executing --> failed : service logic error
    executing --> error : platform / infra error
    succeeded --> [*]
    failed --> [*]
    error --> [*]
Status Meaning scheduled Accepted by the platform, queued for a worker executing Currently running succeeded Completed successfully — results available failed Service logic reported a failure error Platform-level error (infrastructure, timeout, …)

Terminal states: succeeded, failed, error.

docs.title: createAndWait() — Submit and Block Until Done
docs.text:
The simplest path for synchronous workflows. Handles both immediate (HTTP 200) and async (HTTP 202) job creation transparently:

import { IvcapClient, JobResource } from "@ivcap/client";

const client = new IvcapClient();

const job = await client.jobs.createAndWait(
  "urn:ivcap:service:abc-123",
  {
    parameters: JobResource.buildParameters({
      input:     "urn:ivcap:artifact:xyz...",
      threshold: "0.8",
    }),
    name: "My analysis run",
  },
  {
    pollInterval: 5_000,   // poll every 5 seconds (default: 3 000 ms)
    timeout:     300_000,  // throw TimeoutError after 5 min (default: 300 s)
    onUpdate: (j) => console.log("status:", j.status),
  },
);

if (job.status === "succeeded") {
  console.log("Products:", job.products?.items.length ?? 0);
  if (job.resultContent) {
    console.log("Result:", JSON.stringify(job.resultContent, null, 2));
  }
}

docs.title: create() — Submit and Return Immediately
docs.text:
Use create() when you want to fire off a job and handle the sync/async branching yourself. It returns a discriminated union:

const result = await client.jobs.create(serviceId, {
  parameters: [{ name: "input", value: artifactId }],
  name: "background-job",
});

if (result.synchronous) {
  // HTTP 200 — already done
  console.log("Completed inline:", result.job.status);
} else {
  // HTTP 202 — poll later
  console.log("Job ID:    ", result.jobId);
  console.log("Service ID:", result.serviceId);
  if (result.retryLater) {
    console.log(`Retry after: ${result.retryLater}s`);
  }

  // Poll to completion
  const done = await client.jobs.waitUntilDone(
    result.serviceId,
    result.jobId,
    { pollInterval: 5_000, timeout: 300_000 },
  );
  console.log("Final status:", done.status);
}

docs.title: Using buildParameters() Helper
docs.text:
Instead of writing { name, value } pairs manually, use the static helper. It also accepts a plain Record<string, string> directly:

import { JobResource } from "@ivcap/client";

// Helper — converts { key: value } → [{ name, value }, ...]
const params = JobResource.buildParameters({
  input:     "urn:ivcap:artifact:xyz...",
  threshold: "0.8",
  region:    "Tasmania-North",
});

// Or pass the plain object directly — both are equivalent:
const result = await client.jobs.create(serviceId, {
  parameters: { input: "urn:ivcap:artifact:xyz...", threshold: "0.8" },
  name: "quick-run",
});

docs.title: get() — Fetch by Job ID (with automatic bootstrap)
docs.text:
You only need the job URN. The SDK automatically resolves the serviceId from the DataFabric if you don't provide it:

// Bootstrap lookup — only job ID needed (one extra DataFabric round-trip)
const job = await client.jobs.get("urn:ivcap:job:xyz-456");

// Fast path — skip the DataFabric lookup when you already know the service
const job = await client.jobs.get("urn:ivcap:job:xyz-456", {
  serviceId: "urn:ivcap:service:abc-123",
});

console.log(job.status, job.startedAt, job.finishedAt);

docs.title: waitUntilDone() — Poll an Already-Submitted Job
docs.text:
const done = await client.jobs.waitUntilDone(
  serviceId,  // required — use resolveServiceId() if unknown
  jobId,
  {
    pollInterval: 3_000,
    timeout:     600_000,
    onUpdate: (j) => console.log(`[${new Date().toISOString()}] ${j.status}`),
  },
);

docs.title: Listing Jobs
docs.text:
list() queries the DataFabric and returns jobs across all services — no serviceId required:

// Iterate the 20 most recent jobs
for await (const j of client.jobs.list({ limit: 20 })) {
  const svc = j.serviceName ?? j.serviceId;
  console.log(`${j.status.padEnd(12)} ${svc}  ${j.id}`);
}

// Filter to failed jobs using a JSONPath expression
for await (const j of client.jobs.list({
  contentPath: '$.status == "failed"',
})) {
  console.log("failed:", j.id);
}

// Single-page fetch
const page = await client.jobs.listPage({ limit: 10 });
console.log(page.items.map(j => j.id));

docs.title: Inline Result Payload
docs.text:
For services that return small JSON results directly:

const job = await client.jobs.get(jobId);

if (job.resultContent) {
  console.log("Result:", JSON.stringify(job.resultContent, null, 2));
}

docs.title: Large Results (Artifact URN)
docs.text:
Large results are stored as DataFabric artifacts:

if (job.resultContentUrn) {
  const bytes = await client.artifacts.download(job.resultContentUrn);
  console.log("Downloaded", bytes.byteLength, "bytes");
}

docs.title: Products (Output Artifact List)
docs.text:
Many services produce multiple output artifacts listed in job.products.items:

for (const product of job.products?.items ?? []) {
  console.log(product.id, product.mimeType, product.size);

  const bytes = await client.artifacts.download(product.id);
  // ...
}

docs.title: DataFabric Aspects
docs.text:
Every job writes aspects into the DataFabric. Fetch all three in one call:

const aspects = await client.jobs.getAspects(jobId);

// Primary metadata (always present)
console.log(aspects.job?.status, aspects.job?.requestedAt);

// Execution-phase detail (present during / after execution)
console.log(aspects.result?.phase);

// Nextflow-specific results (only for Nextflow jobs)
if (aspects.nextflow) {
  console.log("Pipeline status:", aspects.nextflow.status);
  console.log("Log artifact:  ", aspects.nextflow.logUrn);
  console.log("Process results:", aspects.nextflow.results);
}

docs.title: Real-Time Events (SSE)  (Node.js only)
docs.text:
Stream progress events while a job is running:

// Resolve serviceId if you only have the job URN
const serviceId = await client.jobs.resolveServiceId(jobId);

for await (const event of client.jobs.events(serviceId, jobId)) {
  const ts = event.timestamp ?? new Date().toISOString();
  console.log(`[${ts}] ${event.type ?? "unknown"}`);
  if (event.data) console.log("  ", JSON.stringify(event.data));
}

Resume a dropped stream with lastEventId:

for await (const event of client.jobs.events(serviceId, jobId, {
  lastEventId: lastSeenEventId,
})) {
  // ...
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
import { TimeoutError, NotFoundError, IvcapError } from "@ivcap/client";

try {
  const job = await client.jobs.createAndWait(serviceId, req, {
    timeout: 60_000,
  });

  switch (job.status) {
    case "succeeded":
      console.log("✓ succeeded");
      break;
    case "failed":
      console.error("✗ failed:", job.errorMessage);
      break;
    case "error":
      console.error("✗ platform error — contact support, job:", job.id);
      break;
  }
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof TimeoutError) {
    console.error("Job did not complete within the time limit");
  } else if (err instanceof NotFoundError) {
    console.error("Service not found:", serviceId);
  } else if (err instanceof IvcapError) {
    console.error(`IVCAP error [${err.statusCode}]: ${err.message}`);
  } else {
    throw err;
  }
}

docs.title: Guides Overview
docs.text: These guides provide in-depth explanations and patterns for using the IVCAP Client SDK.

docs.title: Workflow at a Glance
docs.text:
The typical IVCAP workflow follows these steps:

1. List available services      client.services.list()
2. Inspect a service            client.services.get(serviceId)
3. Upload input data            client.artifacts.upload(data, opts)
4. Submit a job                 client.jobs.create(serviceId, req)
5. Poll for completion          client.jobs.waitUntilDone(serviceId, jobId)
   (or combine steps 4 + 5)    client.jobs.createAndWait(serviceId, req)
6. Download result artifacts    client.artifacts.download(productId)

docs.title: Guide Index
docs.text: Guide What you will learn Discovering Services List, search, and inspect analytics services Running Jobs Submit jobs and monitor their lifecycle Working with Artifacts Upload, download, and manage data blobs The Datafabric & Aspects Read/write typed metadata and query provenance Pagination Efficiently iterate over large collections Error Handling Handle typed errors gracefully Advanced Usage Token rotation, low-level HTTP, browser notes

docs.title: Everything is a URN
docs.text:
Every resource in IVCAP has a stable, globally unique identifier:

urn:ivcap:service:<uuid>
urn:ivcap:job:<uuid>
urn:ivcap:artifact:<uuid>
urn:ivcap:aspect:<uuid>
urn:ivcap:queue:<uuid>

Use URNs everywhere you see a parameter typed as URN.

docs.title: Lazy Pagination
docs.text:
list() methods return a PageIterator — an async iterable that fetches pages on demand as you consume items:

// Only fetches pages as you iterate
for await (const artifact of client.artifacts.list()) {
  process(artifact); // pages are fetched in the background
}

docs.title: Jobs are Scoped to Services
docs.text: All job methods require the owning serviceId as their first argument. The REST API paths follow /1/services/{serviceId}/jobs/....

docs.title: Immutable Provenance via Aspects
docs.text: Aspects (metadata records) are never deleted — they are retracted (marked invalid at a point in time). This gives you a full audit trail and enables historical queries.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: All list() methods in the IVCAP SDK return a PageIterator — an async iterable that lazily fetches pages from the API as you consume items.

docs.title: Basic Iteration
docs.text:
The most common pattern is for await...of:

for await (const artifact of client.artifacts.list()) {
  console.log(artifact.id, artifact.name);
}

Pages are fetched automatically in the background only when needed.

docs.title: List Options
docs.text:
All list methods accept an options object with common fields:

Option Type Description limit number Max items per page (server default varies) filter string Server-side filter expression orderBy string Field to sort by orderDesc boolean Descending sort (default: false) atTime DateTimeString Historical query — results at this point in time 
for await (const svc of client.services.list({
  limit:     25,
  orderBy:   "name",
  orderDesc: false,
  search:    "climate",   // services-only option
})) {
  console.log(svc.name);
}

docs.title: .toArray() — Collect All Items
docs.text:
Fetches all remaining pages and returns them as an array:

const all = await client.artifacts.list().toArray();
console.log(`Total: ${all.length} artifacts`);

Memory usage

Be careful with very large collections — all items will be loaded into memory.

docs.title: .firstPage() — Fetch Only the First Page
docs.text:
const first = await client.artifacts.list({ limit: 20 }).firstPage();
console.log(first.map(a => a.name));

docs.title: .forEach() — Callback Style
docs.text:
await client.jobs.list(serviceId).forEach(async (job) => {
  console.log(job.id, job.status);
});

docs.title: collectAll() Utility
docs.text:
The collectAll helper is equivalent to .toArray() and works with any PageIterator:

import { collectAll } from "@ivcap/client";

const allServices = await collectAll(client.services.list());

docs.title: Fetching a Single Page with Cursors
docs.text:
When you need direct control over cursor-based pagination, use listPage():

// First page
const page1 = await client.artifacts.listPage({ limit: 10 });
console.log(page1.items);

// Next page — find the "next" cursor in the links array
const nextLink = page1.links?.find(l => l.rel === "next");
if (nextLink) {
  // Use getNextPage() helper or pass the cursor manually
}

docs.title: getNextPage() Helper
docs.text:
import { getNextPage } from "@ivcap/client";

let page = await client.artifacts.listPage({ limit: 10 });
while (page) {
  page.items.forEach(a => console.log(a.name));
  page = await getNextPage(client.artifacts, page);
}

docs.title: Early Exit
docs.text:
You can break out of a for await loop at any time — no more pages are fetched:

for await (const artifact of client.artifacts.list()) {
  if (artifact.name === "target-file.json") {
    console.log("Found it:", artifact.id);
    break; // stops fetching immediately
  }
}

docs.title: Parallel Processing
docs.text:
Combine lazy iteration with Promise.all for concurrent processing:

const tasks: Promise<void>[] = [];

for await (const artifact of client.artifacts.list({ limit: 100 })) {
  tasks.push(processArtifact(artifact));

  // Process in batches of 10
  if (tasks.length >= 10) {
    await Promise.all(tasks.splice(0, 10));
  }
}

// Flush remaining
await Promise.all(tasks);

docs.title: Discovering Services
docs.text: IVCAP services are registered analytic capabilities — each with a defined parameter schema, description, and lifecycle status. This guide covers how to discover, filter, and inspect them.

docs.title: Listing All Services
docs.text:
The list() method returns a lazy PageIterator that fetches pages as you consume items:

for await (const svc of client.services.list()) {
  console.log(svc.id, svc.name, svc.description);
}

docs.title: Limiting Results
docs.text:
// Only fetch the first 10 services
for await (const svc of client.services.list({ limit: 10 })) {
  console.log(svc.name);
}

docs.title: Free-text Search
docs.text:
// Full-text search across name and description
for await (const svc of client.services.list({ search: "fire risk" })) {
  console.log(svc.id, svc.name);
}

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text:
for await (const svc of client.services.list({
  orderBy:   "name",
  orderDesc: false,
})) {
  console.log(svc.name);
}

docs.title: Collecting All at Once
docs.text:
import { collectAll } from "@ivcap/client";

const allServices = await collectAll(client.services.list());
console.log(`Found ${allServices.length} services`);

docs.title: Fetching a Single Page
docs.text:
Use listPage() when you need direct access to pagination cursors:

const page = await client.services.listPage({ limit: 20 });
console.log(page.items.length, "services on this page");

docs.title: Getting Service Details
docs.text:
Fetch the complete description including the parameter schema:

const svc = await client.services.get("urn:ivcap:service:abc-123");

console.log("Name:       ", svc.name);
console.log("Description:", svc.description);
console.log("Status:     ", svc.status);   // "active" | "inactive" | "error"
console.log("Tags:       ", svc.tags);

// Inspect parameter definitions
svc.parameters.forEach(p => {
  const required = p.optional ? "" : " [required]";
  const def      = p.default  ? ` (default: ${p.default})` : "";
  console.log(`  ${p.name} : ${p.type}${required}${def}`);
  if (p.description) console.log(`    ${p.description}`);
});

docs.title: ServiceDetail Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id URN Unique service identifier name string Human-friendly name description string What the service does status ServiceStatus active | inactive | error parameters ParameterDef[] Input parameter definitions tags string[] Searchable tags policy URN Access policy URN validFrom DateTimeString When the service became valid validTo DateTimeString Expiry time (if any)

docs.title: ParameterDef Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Parameter name (used in job requests) type string Data type (string, artifact, number, …) description string Human description label string? UI label unit string? Physical unit optional boolean? Whether the parameter may be omitted default string? Default value options Array<{value, description}>? Allowed values (enum)

docs.title: Historical Queries
docs.text:
Query the service catalogue as it was at a specific point in time:

const svc = await client.services.listPage({
  atTime: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
});

docs.title: Finding a Service by Name
docs.text:
There is no dedicated "find by name" endpoint; use search + iteration:

async function findServiceByName(
  client: IvcapClient,
  name: string,
): Promise<ServiceDetail | undefined> {
  for await (const svc of client.services.list({ search: name })) {
    if (svc.name === name) return client.services.get(svc.id);
  }
  return undefined;
}

docs.title: Build Your First AI Agent Service
docs.text:
This tutorial gives you a high-level picture of how to build AI agents on IVCAP — services that call an LLM and, crucially, call other IVCAP services as part of their reasoning.

We use the Agent Calling Agent tutorial as the worked example. It builds two cooperating services:

  • Fact Checker — receives a list of references and asks an LLM to assess the credibility and relevance of each one.
  • Report Writer — receives a topic, asks an LLM to write a concise summary, then passes the generated references to the Fact Checker for validation.

The result is a structured report with per-reference assessments attached.

The full, step-by-step tutorial (including all source code) lives here:

github.com/ivcap-works/agent-calling-agent-tutorial

Prerequisite

This tutorial assumes familiarity with the basic IVCAP service development workflow. If you haven't done so yet, start with Build Your First Service.

docs.title: How the two agents cooperate
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant RW as Report Writer
    participant LLM1 as LLM (writer)
    participant FC as Fact Checker
    participant LLM2 as LLM (reviewer)

    User->>RW: topic: "The Solar System"
    RW->>LLM1: write summary + references
    LLM1-->>RW: report text with [1], [2] references

    loop for each reference
        RW->>FC: assess reference [N]
        FC->>LLM2: assess credibility & relevance
        LLM2-->>FC: assessment text
        FC-->>RW: assessment for [N]
    end

    RW-->>User: report + reference assessments

Both services are ordinary IVCAP services — deployed independently, discoverable via ivcap service list, and invokable directly with ivcap job create. The Report Writer discovers and calls the Fact Checker at runtime using the IVCAP agent client built into the service SDK.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Tool Purpose Python 3.9+ Service implementation Poetry + poetry-plugin-ivcap Dependency management and IVCAP tooling Docker Build and test service containers ivcap CLI (installed & authenticated) Deploy services and run jobs Git Version the code Access to an LLM API key Both services call an LLM (OpenAI-compatible)

docs.title: 1 — Each agent is a normal IVCAP service
docs.text: There is no special "agent" runtime. Each agent is a Python function wrapped with ivcap-lambda, containerised, and deployed exactly as in the Build Your First Service tutorial. The @service decorator handles HTTP, schema validation, and platform registration.

docs.title: 2 — The Fact Checker: a stateless LLM wrapper
docs.text:
The simpler of the two services. For each reference it receives, it constructs LLM prompts and returns an assessment:

# system: "You are a critical academic reviewer."
# user:   "Assess the credibility and relevance of this reference: {ref}"

It has no knowledge of the Report Writer — it can be called by any service or directly by a user.

docs.title: 3 — The Report Writer: an agent that calls another agent
docs.text:
After writing the report, the Report Writer extracts references from the LLM output and calls the Fact Checker via IVCAP's agent client, which is injected into the service through JobContext:

def check_references(report_text: str, request: ReportRequest, ctxt: JobContext):
    # Find lines starting with '[' — these are the references
    references = [
        line.strip()
        for line in report_text.splitlines()
        if line.strip().startswith("[")
    ]

    # Resolve the Fact Checker service by its URN
    agent = ctxt.ivcap.get_agent(request.fact_checker.agent_id)

    # Build a typed request and call the agent synchronously
    req = agent.request_model(references=references, ...)
    job = agent.exec_agent(req)

    return job.result["results"]

ctxt.ivcap.get_agent(...) fetches the service definition and exposes a typed client. agent.exec_agent(req) submits a job and waits for the result — the platform handles scheduling, retries, and provenance recording automatically.

docs.title: 4 — Deploy in dependency order
docs.text:
Because the Report Writer needs the Fact Checker's service URN at runtime, deploy the Fact Checker first:

Future: named service discovery

Passing the Fact Checker's URN explicitly at job submission time will not always be necessary. A planned move to named services will allow agents to discover their dependencies dynamically by name at runtime, removing the need to know (or hard-code) a specific service URN in advance.

# In fact_checker/
git add . && git commit -m "fact checker v1"
poetry ivcap deploy

# Note the service URN printed at the end, then:

# In report_writer/
git add . && git commit -m "report writer v1"
poetry ivcap deploy

docs.title: 5 — Run the pipeline
docs.text:
Create a request file solar.json:

{
  "topic": "The Solar System",
  "fact_checker": {
    "agent_id": "urn:ivcap:service:<fact-checker-urn>"
  }
}

Then submit the job:

cd report_writer
poetry ivcap job-exec tests/solar.json

After a few seconds you will get a structured result with the generated report and per-reference credibility assessments:

topic: The Solar System
content: >-
  The Solar System consists of the Sun and all objects bound to it by gravity ...

  References:
  [1] NASA Solar System Exploration - https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/...
  [2] European Space Agency (ESA)   - https://www.esa.int/...

references:
  - reference: "[1] NASA Solar System Exploration - ..."
    assessment: "This reference is highly credible. NASA is a leading authority ..."
  - reference: "[2] European Space Agency (ESA) - ..."
    assessment: "..."

docs.title: Build Your First Service
docs.text:
This tutorial gives you a high-level picture of what it takes to build and deploy an IVCAP service. We use the Gene Ontology (GO) Term Mapper as the worked example — a real service that maps UniProt protein IDs to GO annotations using the QuickGO API.

The full, step-by-step tutorial (including all source code) lives in the example repository:

github.com/ivcap-works/gene-onology-term-mapper

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Tool Purpose Python 3.9+ Service implementation Poetry Dependency and packaging management Docker Build and test the service container ivcap CLI (installed & authenticated) Push the image and register the service Git Version the code (IVCAP uses the commit hash as the service version)

docs.title: What an IVCAP service looks like
docs.text:
An IVCAP service is a containerised HTTP endpoint that:

  1. Accepts a structured JSON request (described by a schema)
  2. Does its work (calling APIs, running models, processing data, …)
  3. Returns a structured JSON result

The ivcap-lambda Python package provides the service wrapper that handles the HTTP layer, schema validation, and automatic registration with the platform.

docs.title: 1 — Implement the core logic
docs.text:
Write the domain function independently of IVCAP. For the GO Term Mapper this is a simple async function that calls the QuickGO REST API and returns typed Pydantic objects:

async def fetch_go_terms(uniprot_id: str) -> List[Annotation]:
    """Fetch GO annotations for a UniProt ID from QuickGO."""
    ...

Having the core logic separate from the service wrapper makes it easy to test locally with plain Python before introducing any IVCAP concepts.

docs.title: 2 — Wrap it as an IVCAP service
docs.text:
Use ivcap-lambda to declare the service, its input/output schemas, and its entrypoint. A minimal wrapper looks like this:

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from ivcap_service import Service, ServiceContact
from ivcap_lambda import ivcap_lambda, start_lambda_server, ToolOptions, logging_init

logging_init()

service = Service(
    name="GO Term Mapper",
    contact=ServiceContact(name="Your Name", email="you@example.com"),
)

@ivcap_lambda("/")
async def map_go_terms(req: Request) -> GOTermResult:
    """Map UniProt protein IDs to GO annotations.

    Calls the QuickGO API and returns structured GO term annotations
    for each supplied UniProt ID.
    """
    results = {}
    for uid in req.ids:
        terms = await fetch_go_terms(uid)
        results[uid] = filter_by_category(terms, req.category)
    return GOTermResult(results=results)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    start_lambda_server(service)

docs.title: 3 — Test locally
docs.text:
Run the service directly with Poetry:

poetry ivcap run

Then call it with curl:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8077 \
     -H "content-type: application/json" \
     --data '{"ids": ["P12345"], "category": "BP"}' | jq

docs.title: 4 — Containerise
docs.text:
Add a Dockerfile and build the image:

poetry ivcap docker-build
poetry ivcap docker-run   # verify the container behaves identically

docs.title: 5 — Deploy to IVCAP
docs.text:
Commit your code (the commit hash becomes the service version), then publish:

git add . && git commit -m "initial release"
poetry ivcap deploy

This single command:

  • Builds a platform-native Docker image
  • Pushes it to the IVCAP package registry
  • Registers the service definition on the platform
  • Registers the service as a discoverable tool

After a successful deploy you can submit jobs immediately:

ivcap job create urn:ivcap:service:<your-service-id> \
    -f go_request.json --watch
